body:
A block id that is stored in the metadata of a database file is used without looking at it. Two cases, both hit by `ATTACH` of a corrupt file:

* The pointer to the next block of a metadata chain holds a very large block id. `SingleFileBlockManager::GetBlockLocation` multiplies the id with the block size, which wraps around. `DatabaseHandle::Read` then decides whether the read can be served from the prefetched header with `location + block.AllocSize() <= prefetched_header->size()`. That sum wraps as well, the check passes, and one block is copied from outside of the prefetched header buffer. AddressSanitizer reports the read; a release build reports a checksum mismatch over whatever memory was copied (the numbers in the message differ from run to run).
* The list of metadata blocks that is stored with the free list holds a block id in the range of in-memory blocks: `INTERNAL Error: AddAndRegisterBlock called with a transient block id`, which invalidates the instance.

With this PR:

* `GetBlockLocation` throws `Data Corruption Error: Corrupt database file: block id <id> is out of range` when the location of the block or its end does not fit.
* The check in `DatabaseHandle::Read` no longer adds to the location.
* `MetadataManager::Read` throws `Data Corruption Error: Corrupt database file: invalid metadata block id <id>` for an id that is negative or in the range of in-memory blocks.

A block id that is in range but past the end of the file is not touched here: reading it already fails with a regular error.

### Test

`test/sql/storage/corrupt/block_id_out_of_range.test` attaches one file per case (`data/storage/corrupt/block_id_location_overflow.db.gz`, `metadata_block_id_transient.db.gz`, 4 KB and 3 KB) and checks that the instance is still usable afterwards. Both files were found by fuzzing the storage reader. The test also passes under AddressSanitizer, which reported the out-of-bounds read for the first file before the fix.



Note: this PR was generated by an AI coding agent.
title: Reject out-of-range block ids read from a database file
